title: Fundamental Mean Reversion instance configuration
description: Reaches the manager as ManagerInvocation.config. ⚠️ Nothing here can loosen this methodology: the discovery gate, the stabilisation test and the target-basis rules are not configurable at all, and the two settings that touch risk may only be narrowed — a value looser than the pre-registered one is refused, reported, and the pre-registered one governs. Every value here is also written into PROMPT.md, because an invocation may carry no config block at all.

perThesisRiskBudget.description: Fraction of the fund's net asset value this methodology is willing to lose on one thesis reaching its invalidation, after the gap and halt haircuts. The ceiling is the pre-registered 0.0075 and a larger value is refused: at a 20% effective loss it produces a 3.75% position, so eight open theses put roughly 6% of the book at risk. Lower it to run smaller; there is no way to raise it here.

maxWaitDays.description: Calendar days a thesis may wait for the recovery before the position is re-judged in the open. The ceiling is the pre-registered 120 — roughly the upper end of the weeks-to-months window this methodology researches — and each thesis still names its own shorter deadline first. This is the ceiling on what a thesis may name, not a default the run may fall back to instead of naming one.

maxOpenTheses.description: How many mean-reversion theses this manager will carry at once. It is a ceiling on attention rather than on risk: a thesis this methodology cannot review properly after the close is a stop nobody is watching. The account's own concentration and gross limits are the Mandate's and are never derived from this number.

researchShortlistSize.description: How many candidates a discovery pass carries forward. Deliberately small: #256 forbids ending a run with a shallow pass over many promising names, so the shortlist is sized to what one run can finish rather than to what the screen returned. ⚠️ This is a hard cut in `discoveryRun` and not an intention: names past it are reported as truncated with their open questions, never as rejections.

discoveryBudgetSymbols.description: How many symbols of the declared universe one run reads adjusted daily bars for. It bounds the sweep rather than the methodology: the roster is swept incrementally from the last successful cursor, so a smaller budget reaches the whole market more slowly and never reaches less of it. ⚠️ A budget that consumes the run before any candidate is researched is the failure #256 names, which is why `researchCompletionFloor` sits beside it.

researchCompletionFloor.description: How many shortlisted candidates a run must research to a finished answer before it may end. ⛔ Reading many names shallowly and stopping is forbidden by #256 outright; this is the floor that makes it reportable. A run that reaches the end with fewer says so in its own record rather than presenting the shortlist as work done.
